thread:
mike (Support): FYI Everest Analytics is hitting 429s and auth errors on their dedicated pool since ~08:10 UTC. Tickets inbound, customer is seeing elevated latency too.
eli (SRE): Can you paste their baseline vs observed QPS and the pool config? 429s usually mean we hit the per-pool throttle or autoscale didn't keep up.
maria (CS): Baseline reported ~160 qps steady. Peak bursts yesterday reached ~1.9k qps for ~6–8m, today similar pattern. They said embedding jobs started during the burst.
eli (SRE): Thanks. Do we have the pool size and autoscale settings? Also any token/auth errors logs (401/403)?
mike (Support): Pool: dedicated-evr-01, 6 nodes (A100-equivalent), autoscale min=6 max=18, policy target_util=0.7, warmup disabled. No explicit 401s in the support logs — a handful of token validation timeouts showed up around 08:12 but the majority are 429.
jaya (eng-runtime): That target_util=0.7 with min=6 looks low for 2k qps peaks. If each node sustains ~300 qps for their mix, 6 nodes -> 1.8k headroom is thin and batching shifts can push util >> target. We probably saw queue growth -> throttles.
eli (SRE): Can someone grab the recent allocator/serving metrics? I want: per-node qps, queue length over time, and throttle_count metric.
mike (Support): Pasted partial metrics from the console graph:
```
08:05 - qps total: 180
08:10 - qps total: 1750
08:12 - qps total: 1960
08:14 - qps total: 400
throttle_count: 482 (08:10-08:16)
avg_p90_latency: 420ms -> spikes to 2.1s at peak
node_utilization: nodes 1-4: 92%, nodes 5-6: 88%
```
eli (SRE): That matches autoscale not reacting fast enough. Also shows sustained node util > target. Noisy neighbor is likely — embeddings are heavy. Any logs showing a single tenant dominating bytes/tokens?
maria (CS): Everest confirms they kicked off a large nightly embedding backfill at 08:06 which overlapped production traffic. They were running 8 concurrent workers with large batch sizes.
samir (Everest Analytics): yup, we started a backfill and didn't expect it to coincide with product traffic. Sorry for the outage. We paused the backfill at 08:18.
jaya (eng-runtime): Quick reproducer to check throttles locally (for SRE):
```
# reproduce load pattern: 8 concurrent clients, 256 batch size
for i in {1..8}; do
  while true; do
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $EVR_TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","input":"x"}' &
  done &
done
```
eli (SRE): Logs from the serving runtime show throttles triggered by token bucket on the pool level: `pool_throttle_events: 472` and `autoscale_actions: scale_up_requested` but scale up lag ~90s due to cooldown. Also saw long KV cache spills during the embedding job which increased CPU/IO on GPU host.
mike (Support): Customer also reported a few `auth: rate limit exceeded` errors — looks like their token issuer returned 502 during the heavy job start; some calls got 401 transiently. Not systemic to our auth layer.
jaya (eng-runtime): Immediate mitigation suggestions:
- Set a temporary soft quota on that tenant to limit background embedding job concurrency (we can do a per-tenant throttle policy).
- Increase autoscale max to 30 for 1 hour to accommodate bursts.
- Lower target_util to 0.6 so autoscaler triggers earlier.
- Enable warmup window (pre-warm new nodes) to reduce scale-up lag.
- Suggest customer reduce embedding batch size to 64 for backfills.

maria (CS): I'll ask Everest to lower workers to 2 concurrently for the rest of the day and switch to smaller batches. They agreed to the change.
eli (SRE): For a medium-term fix: recommend resizing reserved capacity for them from 6 -> 12 nodes (or convert to a burstable reserved slab). With baseline 160 qps and predictable nightly backfills, target_util 0.6 and headroom for 2k qps peaks implies ~12 nodes. Calculation: required_nodes ≈ peak_qps / node_capacity -> 2000 / 300 ≈ 6.7, but want headroom + embeddings noise -> 12 recommended.
mike (Support): I'll open a PR with proposed reserved plan and pricing options.
samir (Everest Analytics): For the short term, please apply the soft quota and bump autoscale max. We need assurances this won't happen again.
eli (SRE): Done: applied per-tenant soft quota (concurrency cap 4) at 08:30 UTC, raised autoscale max to 30 for pool dedicated-evr-01, lowered scd target_util to 0.6. We'll monitor for 2 hours.
ops-bot: Ticket #SUP-2026-982 created and linked to internal incident IN-2026-311. Alert rule: dedicated_pool_utilization > 85% for 5m.
maria (CS): Everest confirmed errors dropped after pause + our changes. They still want a postmortem and an action plan.
jaya (eng-runtime): Action items:
- (eli) Collect final traces and produce timeline + autoscale logs (ETA 24h).
- (jaya) Propose default autoscale policy adjustments for backfill patterns and add tenant-level safeguards (ETA 3 days).
- (mike) Draft customer-facing RCA and reserved capacity proposal (ETA 48h).
eli (SRE): Adding notes: consider adding an autoscale fast-path for sudden spikes (aggressive short-lived ramp with cost guardrails).
mike (Support): Thanks everyone. I'll keep Everest in the loop. Closing thread when RCA doc is uploaded. :thumbsup:
